finish_summary: Explored several equivalent restructurings of the 32-bit unsigned comparator (bit-pairwise priority tree, subtraction-based magnitude compare, cleaned-up baseline, and a nibble-granularity priority-encode tree) using estimate_ppa to screen cheaply before spending place_and_route budget. Verified functional equivalence via simulate (including a caught/fixed indexing bug in an early tree attempt) and prove_equivalence (formal sequential equivalence, PROVEN) for the final candidate. The winning design computes per-nibble (4-bit) less-than/equal signals directly via '<' and '==' on 4-bit slices, then combines them with a compact 3-level priority-merge tree (nibble->2-nibble->4-nibble->final) instead of the flat 32-bit '<' operator relied on by the reference. This gave the best measured place_and_route result: area 268.394 um^2 (vs 268.926 baseline), WNS 7.6378 ns (vs 7.62112 baseline), score 76.109606 vs baseline 75.942274 (+0.167332). Other variants (bit-pair binary tree, subtraction-based) scored worse in estimate_ppa and were not submitted to the limited place_and_route budget. This nibble-tree result is the best verified submission and is used as the final score.
